caption:
The video captures a fixed, wide view of a mountain valley bathed in golden-hour light, where a bright sun hangs near the top center above layered, hazy ridges. Throughout the excerpt the sun remains stationary, its white core and surrounding halo maintaining a constant intensity. The warm glow spreads across the pale sky without changing. A thick sea of fog fills the valley floor, and a dark rock pinnacle protrudes from it near the center, holding its position.

The fog surface remains still, a smooth bright band in the center holding its shape while the right side shows wispy streams across the slope. The overall fog level and the dark pinnacle stay in place, and the sky tone remains constant. The leafless tree on the left, the bottom foliage, the mountain silhouettes, and the two-pole structure on the right ridge stay locked to the frame. This confirms the entire scene is completely static.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.

draft_caption:
The video captures a fixed, wide view of a mountain valley bathed in golden-hour light, where a bright sun already hangs near the top center above layered, hazy ridges. Throughout the excerpt the sun climbs steadily upward, its white core and surrounding halo intensifying at a rate far faster than real time. The warm glow spreads across the pale sky as the ascent continues. A thick sea of fog fills the valley floor, and a dark rock pinnacle protrudes from it near the center, holding its position.

The fog surface slowly reorganizes, a smooth bright band in the center shifting while the right side develops wispy streams drifting across the slope. The overall fog level and the dark pinnacle stay in place, and the sky tone warms as the glow spreads. The leafless tree on the left, the bottom foliage, the mountain silhouettes, and the two-pole structure on the right ridge stay locked to the frame. This confirms the visible changes come from object motion rather than any camera pan or zoom.
